In the RaMP multi-database ORA, five steroids—dehydroepiandrosterone (DHEA), testosterone, androstenedione, estrone, and dihydrotestosterone (DHT)—produced one of the strongest pathway enrichments observed in the dataset, with fold-enrichment exceeding 2500× and FDR below 1×10⁻¹⁴ across WikiPathways, KEGG, SMPDB, and Reactome namespaces simultaneously. MetaboAnalystR's KEGG-specific PSEA corroborated the same five steroids mapping to hsa00140. react_result.final_narrative_text: The three enrichment paradigms converge on a single dominant biological signal: steroid hormone biosynthesis and metabolism. In the RaMP multi-database ORA, five steroids—dehydroepiandrosterone (DHEA), testosterone, androstenedione, estrone, and dihydrotestosterone (DHT)—produced one of the strongest pathway enrichments observed in the dataset, with fold-enrichment exceeding 2500× and FDR below 1×10⁻¹⁴ across WikiPathways, KEGG, SMPDB, and Reactome namespaces simultaneously. The KEGG:hsa00140 'Androgen and Estrogen Metabolism' pathway and the WikiPathways 'Steroid biosynthesis' module captured all five driver compounds, as did the broader Reactome 'Metabolism of steroid hormones' and 'Androgen biosynthesis' entries. The mummichog m/z-direct network analysis, which does not depend on compound ID resolution, independently ranked C21-steroid hormone biosynthesis and androgen/estrogen biosynthesis as its top two hits (p=8.4×10⁻⁵ and p=2.5×10⁻⁴), confirming the signal through empirical mass-frequency matching. MetaboAnalystR's KEGG-specific PSEA corroborated the same five steroids mapping to hsa00140. The five steroids share a common substrate pool (cholesterol → pregnenolone → 17α-hydroxyprogesterone or DHEA) and are linked by sequential hydroxysteroid dehydrogenases and CYP450 enzymes; DHEA is the upstream precursor for both testosterone and estrone, and androstenedione sits at the branchpoint between androgen and estrogen arms. No non-steroid metabolite (coumarin, doxycycline, pyrocatechol, spironolactone, 3-hydroxy-L-proline) reached significance in any paradigm, indicating the treatment perturbation is selective for the steroidogenic axis rather than xenobiotic or amino-acid metabolism.

These five compounds appear as hits in three independent pathway enrichments reported by run_ramp_enrichment (WP:WP496 'Steroid biosynthesis', FDR=1.01e-15; KEGG:map00150 'Androgen and Estrogen Metabolism', FDR=2.95e-14; REACT:R-HSA-196071 'Metabolism of steroid hormones', FDR=1.84e-13) and independently in run_mummichog (MUMM:c21_steroid_hormone_biosynthesis_and_metabolism, rank 0, p=0.00025; MUMM:androgen_and_estrogen_biosynthesis_and_metabolism, rank 1, p=0.00042). The five-hit overlap is consistent across ORA and m/z-direct paradigms, confirming genuine steroidogenic disruption rather than a methodological artefact. DHEA serves as the upstream precursor; androstenedione and estrone are branch-point intermediates; testosterone and dihydrotestosterone represent the terminal androgen products. The remaining five metabolites (coumarin, spironolactone, 3-hydroxy-L-proline, pyrocatechol, doxycycline) were not captured in any enriched pathway and likely represent treatment-specific co-exposures or background signals. Cross-paradigm consensus on the steroid module is strong; the absence of hits for non-steroid inputs is consistent across tools.

react_result.final_narrative_text: Three complementary pathway-enrichment paradigms converge on a single dominant biological signal: perturbation of steroid hormone metabolism. RaMP multi-DB ORA (FDR ≈ 10⁻¹⁵) ranks 'Steroid biosynthesis' (WP:WP496) and 'Androgen and Estrogen Metabolism' (WP:WP2263 / KEGG:map00150 / SMPDB:SMP00068) at the very top, with five driver steroids — dehydroepiandrosterone (DHEA), testosterone, androstenedione, estrone, and 17β-hydroxy-5α-androstan-3-one (dihydrotestosterone, DHT) — hitting these pathways. Mummichog m/z-direct analysis independently recovers the same axis as its top two hits (MUMM:c21_steroid_hormone_biosynthesis_and_metabolism, p = 0.0005; MUMM:androgen_and_estrogen_biosynthesis_and_metabolism, p = 0.0008), with complete overlap of all five input steroids. MetaboAnalystR PSEA returns KEGG:hsa00140 as a single weak hit (p = 1.0, null result) — the KEGG pathway background was too diffuse to resolve significance from these ten compounds alone, highlighting the value of multi-paradigm triangulation. The remaining five input metabolites (coumarin, spironolactone, 3-hydroxy-L-proline, pyrocatechol, doxycycline) do not map meaningfully onto the steroid axis; coumarin appears in Mummichog's xenobiotics-metabolism module as a marginal hit, while 3-hydroxy-L-proline and pyrocatechol surface weakly in histidine/tyrosine metabolism. The core biological story is therefore a coordinated shift in C18-C19 steroid homeostasis, implicating androgen and estrogen biosynthesis and interconversion as the primary affected process.

final_react_result.final_narrative_text: The three enrichment paradigms converge on a single dominant biological signal: steroid hormone biosynthesis and metabolism. In the RaMP multi-database ORA, five steroids—dehydroepiandrosterone (DHEA), testosterone, androstenedione, estrone, and dihydrotestosterone (DHT)—produced one of the strongest pathway enrichments observed in the dataset, with fold-enrichment exceeding 2500× and FDR below 1×10⁻¹⁴ across WikiPathways, KEGG, SMPDB, and Reactome namespaces simultaneously. The KEGG:hsa00140 'Androgen and Estrogen Metabolism' pathway and the WikiPathways 'Steroid biosynthesis' module captured all five driver compounds, as did the broader Reactome 'Metabolism of steroid hormones' and 'Androgen biosynthesis' entries. The mummichog m/z-direct network analysis, which does not depend on compound ID resolution, independently ranked C21-steroid hormone biosynthesis and androgen/estrogen biosynthesis as its top two hits (p=8.4×10⁻⁵ and p=2.5×10⁻⁴), confirming the signal through empirical mass-frequency matching. No non-steroid metabolite (coumarin, doxycycline, pyrocatechol, spironolactone, 3-hydroxy-L-proline) reached significance in any paradigm, indicating the treatment perturbation is selective for the steroidogenic axis rather than xenobiotic or amino-acid metabolism.
